main_text.l: Simile ignotus eapris[?], nec lasus aratro, Quem mulcet Zephyri, firmat Sol, excitat imber, Mox Austri tactus flatu, Boreæ ve nivalis, Arescit moriens, & prono pondere corpus Deflectens, post se vestigia nulla relinquit.

At Domini bonitas omnes perdurat in annos, Quæ sibi devotos complectitur. Eius in ævum Iustitia, & quotquot sunt sæcla futura, manebit Erga hos, qui priscum formidant rumpere fœdus, Et seruare studeant sancitas fulmine leges.
Sedes est Domini cælum, regumq; vocatur Rex merito, ut totum nutu qui temperet orbem.
Aligeri, Dominum vestrum celebrate, ministri, Magnanimi heroes: Domini explorare quid optet, Est labor: at vobis mandata capessere fas est.

Vos etiam ætherea Dominum laudate cohortes, Vosq; omnes Domini servi, famuliq; fideles, Vosq; creaturæ Dominum celebrate potentem, Vosq; opera, in vasto struxit quæ plurima mundo, Mens mea, prōpta[?] Deū meritis, age, laudibus effer.
Quum me solliciti angerent dolores, Et rebus Dominum vocavi in arctis, Is meos gemitus, meas querelas,

page.notes: Doubtful readings: "eapris" (line 1 of the first stanza) is unclear and may be "capris" or another word; "prōpta" (last stanza, line 5) is uncertain, the macron over the o may stand for an abbreviation; "studeant" in the second stanza may be "student", the scan is not clear. The long s is printed as f in this typeface and is rendered as plain s. The verse uses the printer's u/v forms, which were normalised to v where consonantal. The first stanza continues from the previous page. The psalm heading is a division of the work, level 1, caput 120.
